correctness.rationale: The reciprocal \(y=1/p\) obeys \(y'=-r(t)y+2\). Symmetric smooth ramps have exactly unit homogeneous multipliers and additive increments between \(2\eta e^{-\eta}\) and \(2\eta e^{\eta}\). Composing the four cycle segments gives \(y_{n+1}=q_ny_n+b_n\), with \(q_n=e^{H_n-F_n}\to e^{-\delta}\) and \(b_n\to2(1+e^{-\delta})\). A strict affine contraction for \(\delta>0\) gives the exact reciprocal limit and hence the positive peak. For \(\delta<0\) the recurrence expands; for \(\delta=0\), its asymptotically unit multiplier and strictly positive forcing imply divergence. Monotone long plateaux and vanishing ramp widths establish the continuous-time upper and lower limits. Arbitrarily long constant plateaux force Bohl exponents \(-1\) and \(+1\). In the balanced linear calendar, \(q_n=1\) and summable \(b_n-4\) give \(y_n=4n+O(1)\). Standalone finite tests passed but cannot prove infinite limits.

value.rationale: Mixed-sign Bohl exponents cannot decide persistence in the general model. The sharp necessary-and-sufficient \(\delta\) boundary resolves the distinction for a motivated smooth two-season family: every favorable-hostile duration pair tends to infinity but an asymptotic difference of order \(1\) changes the population outcome. The exact peak \(\tfrac12\tanh(\delta/2)\) and critical \(n^{-1}\) decline quantify effects hidden from the unchanged Bohl extremes. This addresses a documented mixed-sign gap rather than an arbitrary computed slice.
